title: flows.json
description: What the flow map reads: the screens of a project, the stories that walk them, and where the data lives. The values a screen is drawn in come from the design system stage, not from this file.

project.description: The name of the project, put in the page title.

readAt.description: Where the screens were read from, so a reader can tell how old the map is.

repository.description: The address a source path links into.

screens.description: Every screen, by the name a story refers to it with.

stories.description: What a person does, as a walk over the screens.

name.description: What a person calls this screen.

surface.description: Which frame it is drawn in: a phone for mobile, a browser for web.

status.description: How far this screen has got.

route.description: The path that opens it. A web frame reads it in the address bar.

source.description: The files it was read from, separated by a comma and a space.

ref.description: The step of the path that builds it.

q.description: The open question, on a screen whose status is gap.

html.description: The markup of the body of this screen, written in the design system of the project. The page composes it into a document of its own and draws it in a frame that runs no script of the session.

viewport.description: The size the screen was written at. A screen that names none is written at the size of its surface: 390 by 844 on a phone, 1280 by 800 in a browser.

el.description: The shapes on the screen, from the top down.

element.description: One shape on a screen. It names the kind of shape and the component it stands for, so a building session can read which component goes where.

component.description: The name of the library component this shape stands for, for example Button.

to.description: The screen this shape opens when a person presses it.

active.description: Which item of a nav or a dock is the one being read.

multi.description: More than one option may be chosen.

v.description: What the shape says. A string, a list of strings, or a list of items with v and to.

steps.description: How long the walk is, in the words a person would use.

start.description: The screen the prototype opens on.

lanes.description: A name for each row of the map.

nodes.description: Each screen of the story, with the column and the row it sits at.

edges.description: A way from one screen to another: from, to, what it is called, and how far it has got.

dataModel.description: Where the data lives. The Data view is hidden when this is absent.
